name: Stethacanthus
provenance: Late Devonian, upper Famennian Cleveland Shale, Ohio, USA
description: Small early chondrichthyan with opposed cranial and dorsal denticle fields, a spine-supported brush complex, slender pectoral fin whips and a sweeping epicercal tail.

sources.title: Ginter and Sun (2007), p.710: CMNH 8988 spine-brush and teeth, upper Famennian Cleveland Shale; questions S. altonensis assignment
Zangerl (1984), spine-brush anatomy and opposing denticle fields; comparative anatomy, functional interpretation hypothetical
Lund (1984), stethacanthid spine and paired-fin comparisons, not a Devonian specimen substitution
Ginter (2018), Devonian–Permian symmoriiform record and comparative morphology

notes: Devonian provenance anchor: spine-brush CMNH 8988 and associated teeth from upper Famennian Cleveland Shale. Ginter and Sun (2007, p.710) question its old S. altonensis assignment; consequently labelled Stethacanthus sp., not Akmonistion zangerli.

A comparative whole-animal reconstruction around partial Devonian material, not a complete specimen scan. The selected 0.7 m presentation length is an illustrative small individual, not a measured CMNH 8988 total length or a species maximum.

Oppositely directed enlarged cranial and brush denticles, membranous brush supported by an anterior spine, cladodont five-cusped dentition, long metapterygial pectoral whips and soft epicercal tail distinguish the model. Body proportions, fin whip extent, pigmentation and fine surface detail are reconstructed.

The brush is not hair. Tissue histology and inflation, deterrence or courtship hypotheses do not establish behaviour. This complex-bearing reconstruction does not establish the sex or developmental stage of CMNH 8988, nor claim every individual bore this structure.

Ability is a restrained posture displaying head and brush; only the basal rigid complex rotates. It does not inflate or shed. All animation is artistic compatibility work, not Devonian gameplay specification. Growth is relaxed fin and breathing motion.
